lead: Oregon plumbing deals with rain, soft water, older homes and an occasional hard freeze. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers from Portland to Bend.
risk: older pipes and sewer lines in Portland homes, wet-season drain and sump problems and frozen pipes in cold snaps
risk_short: old pipes, wet basements and frozen pipes
why: Western Oregon's long wet season keeps soil saturated, which strains sump pumps, crawl-space drains and sewer lines. Older Portland and Salem homes often have galvanized supply lines and clay or cast-iron sewer laterals full of roots.

Water here is mostly soft, which can be more corrosive to copper pipe. East of the Cascades, Bend and the high desert have cold winters. Oregon licenses plumbers through the Building Codes Division, and contractors also register with the Construction Contractors Board.
problems: Wet crawl spaces and sump pumps
Western Oregon in the rainy season
tips: Check your sump pump before the rainy season.
Have the sewer line scoped before buying an older home.
Insulate crawl-space pipes before a cold snap.
areas: Calls come from Portland and its suburbs, Salem, Eugene, Bend, Medford, the coast and Eastern Oregon.

faq.a: Oregon's Building Codes Division licenses plumbers, and plumbing businesses must also be licensed by the Construction Contractors Board. Check both before work starts.
